_about: Demand (PRD, "Four demand bars" and "Pacing"). Set by M3-01 and given its ratios by M3-06. Every value here is a starting value with no source behind it, to tune in M3-21. Each bar runs from -100 to 100 and is the sum of its parts, one per input. Each input is a ratio of running totals from 0 up, and each weight is the bar points one whole unit of its input is worth: an input that raises the bar has a weight of 0 or more, and one that lowers it 0 or less. Residential reads open jobs and unemployed workers, each per worker. Commercial reads spending power (residents weighted by `spendingByWealth`): the shop jobs that spending keeps busy, `shopJobsPerSpending` to a unit of it and at most one per worker, less the shop jobs there are, per shop job it keeps busy; then workers without a job, per worker; then shop jobs beyond what the spending keeps busy, per shop job. Office reads medium and high education workers without an office job, per worker, and the office jobs residents and businesses would buy, `officeJobsPerBuyer` to each resident and each shop or factory job, less the office jobs there are, per office job they would buy. Industrial reads unemployed low and medium education workers, per worker; the factory jobs shops need goods from, `factoryJobsPerShopJob` to a shop job, less the factory jobs there are, per factory job they need; and open office jobs, per worker, which lower it so a dense city leans on offices. Industrial reads nothing above 0 while no road the player built reaches an outside connection. A bar whose parts add up to more than 100 either way has them scaled down together. `dailyShare` is how far each part moves toward its new value each game day, so bars do not flicker. `outsidePull` holds the residential bar's target at least at `bar` until the city has `untilResidents` residents, so the first houses always come (M3-06). `buildingsPerDayAtFullDemand` is, for each zone, how many buildings the grower adds a game day with its bar at 100 (M3-07): a zone builds only while its bar is above zero, at its rate times the bar over 100, rounded up, so a bar barely above zero still builds one a day. Mixed has no bar and reads the lower of residential and commercial. Starting values to tune in M3-21: on an empty city a 192 m street zoned R1 six deep on both sides fills in about a game week, while the residential bar climbs toward the outside pull's 25. `arrivalsPerYearAtFullDemand` is how many residents move in a game year with the residential bar at 100, about 17,000 from "Pacing" in the PRD; fewer come as the bar falls, and none while it is at or below zero (M3-08). `emptyRoomShareMax` holds new homes back while the room empty in homes newcomers can reach is more than that share of those homes' room, so free room fills before more is built (M3-08, PRD "Turnover"). `openJobsShareMax` does the same for workplaces (M3-09): the grower adds no building to a zone that offers jobs while the open jobs in that zone's buildings, counting those on a road that reaches an outside connection, are more than that share of their jobs. `jobMatching` weights the workplaces a pop looking for work draws among (M3-09, PRD "Job matching"): each open job its education allows counts 1 / (1 + (t / `halfWeightSeconds`)^`falloffPower`), t the free-flow seconds from the pop's home, so a job `halfWeightSeconds` away counts half as much as one next door, and a larger whole `falloffPower` makes the weight fall away faster beyond that. Residential also reads its residents' average satisfaction, weighted by pop size, less `satisfactionNeutral`, over 100 (M3-10): residents happier than that raise the bar and unhappier ones lower it, and a city with no residents reads 0. `departuresPerYearAtFullDemand` is how many residents leave a game year with the residential bar at -100, the least satisfied first; fewer go as the bar rises, and none while it is at or above zero (M3-10, PRD "Satisfaction"). No prices here, so no source years.
